thig2.3:1.1: This verse is problematic and any translation is conjectural. I think that, like [thig1.11](), it hinges on double entendres of kitchen drudgery and sex. The nun here is presumably the mother of the Sumaṅgala at [thag1.43](), whose verses are similar.
thig2.3:1.3: If _vāpi_ is emended to _vāti_ (or _vāyi_), it refers to his erection, of which wind is a cause ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj1:10.17.6]()), cf. Rig Veda 1.28.6). Otherwise it is emphatic, “My husband was most certainly a mushroom”.
thig2.3:1.4: For “mortar” (_ukkhalikā_), compare Sanskrit _ulūkhala_ (or _ulūkhalaka_) in the erotic hymn Rig Veda 1.28, and also Śathapatha Brāhmaṇa 7.5.1.22, “the mortar is the womb of all breaths”. If the sense “little cauldron” is preferred, see ŚB 6.6.2.8, “the cauldron is female, the fire male” (also 7.1.1.42). | For _vāti_ in the sense, “emitted an odor”, see _vāyinī_ in Pv-a 2.3.
